input.quote: Risk of loss for all Base Components shall at all times remain with IBM. Risk of loss for all Customer Components shall at all times remain with Customer.
input.rationale: The Agreement contains no insurance provision (a document-wide search for "insurance" returns nothing, and the outline has no insurance heading). IBM is a hosting/services provider that stores Customer Components and processes personal information on Customer's behalf (§ 5.3 Security; § 14.18 Data Protection), so the playbook requires standard coverages. Risk of Loss (§ 14.12) is the nearest related clause, so a new § 14.12A Insurance is inserted immediately after it, requiring CGL of USD 1M/2M, E&O of USD 2M, cyber liability of USD 5M and statutory workers' compensation, with certificates on request. Fallback of E&O USD 1M / cyber USD 2M is offered in the comment.

ops.text: Insurance

IBM shall maintain, at its own expense, throughout the term of this Agreement and for one (1) year thereafter: commercial general liability insurance of not less than USD 1,000,000 per occurrence and USD 2,000,000 in the aggregate; professional liability (errors and omissions) insurance of not less than USD 2,000,000; cyber liability insurance of not less than USD 5,000,000 covering IBM's processing of Customer data; and workers' compensation insurance as required by applicable law. IBM shall provide Customer with certificates of insurance evidencing such coverage upon request.

proposal.comment: [Playbook] We added a standard insurance provision because IBM hosts and processes our data but the Agreement is silent on coverage. Our position is commercial general liability of USD 1M/2M, E&O of USD 2M and cyber liability of USD 5M with certificates on request; we can accept E&O of USD 1M and cyber of USD 2M if needed.

input.rationale: The Agreement contains no insurance provision (a document-wide search for "insurance" returns nothing, and the outline has no insurance heading). IBM is a hosting/services provider that stores Customer Components and processes personal information on Customer's behalf (§ 5.3 Security; § 14.18 Data Protection), so the playbook requires standard coverages. Risk of Loss (§ 14.12) is the nearest related clause, so a new § 14.12A Insurance is inserted immediately after it, requiring CGL of USD 1M/2M, E&O of USD 2M, cyber liability of USD 5M and statutory workers' compensation, with certificates on request. Fallback of E&O USD 1M / cyber USD 2M is offered in the comment.

Parties: we represent Bluefly, Inc. (Customer); counterparty is International Business Machines Corporation (IBM).

Rule:
ID: LD
Title: Liquidated damages and penalties payable by Customer
Kind: direction
Summary: Service credits to us are welcome; liquidated damages against us are not.
Severity: high
Category: commercial
Position — preferred:
No liquidated damages or penalties payable by Customer.
Position — fallback:
Early-termination fee capped at 3 months' fees as the sole liquidated amount.
Position — walk-away:
Liquidated damages exceeding the remaining contract value or triggered by minor breaches.
Detection guidance:
Identify liquidated damages, penalties, minimum fees on termination, "shall pay … as liquidated damages". Flag only when Customer pays. Service credits or LDs payable by Vendor to Customer are compliant.

Redline guidance:
Delete the Customer-payable LD; if an early-termination fee is unavoidable, cap it at 3 months' fees.

Rule:
ID: TRANSITION
Title: Post-termination transition assistance and data return
Kind: missing
Summary: When it ends, we get our data back and help moving.
Severity: medium
Category: transition
Position — preferred:
On expiry or termination, Vendor provides transition assistance for up to 6 months at then-current rates, returns Customer Data in a standard machine-readable format within 30 days, and certifies deletion thereafter.

Position — fallback:
90 days of transition assistance; data export within 30 days.
Position — walk-away:
No data return, or immediate deletion of Customer Data on termination.
Detection guidance:
Look for transition, exit, data return/export, deletion timing. Absence in a services/hosting agreement is a deviation (insert).
Redline guidance:
Insert a transition-assistance and data-return paragraph in the termination section.
Model language:
Upon expiry or termination of this Agreement for any reason, Vendor shall (a) at Customer's request, provide reasonable transition assistance for up to six (6) months at Vendor's then-current rates; (b) within thirty (30) days, return all Customer Data in a commonly used, machine-readable format; and (c) thereafter delete Customer Data from its systems and certify such deletion in writing.

Parties: we represent Bluefly, Inc. (Customer); counterparty is International Business Machines Corporation (IBM).

Rule:
ID: WARRANTY
Title: Performance warranty and duration
Kind: parametric
Summary: The Vendor must stand behind its work for a meaningful period with a real remedy.
Severity: medium
Category: warranty
Position — preferred:
Services performed in a professional and workmanlike manner; deliverables/software conform to documentation for 12 months (software) or 90 days (services) with repair, replace or refund; compliance with laws; no malicious code.

Position — fallback:
90 days for software, 30 days for services; same remedies.
Position — walk-away:
"AS IS" with all warranties disclaimed and no conformance warranty at all.
Detection guidance:
Find warranty and disclaimer sections; extract the warranty period and remedy; note whether the disclaimer swallows the express warranty. A missing express warranty is a deviation (insert).

Redline guidance:
Extend the period, add the remedy sentence, carve the express warranty out of the disclaimer.
Model language:
Vendor warrants that (a) the Services will be performed in a professional and workmanlike manner consistent with industry standards; and (b) for a period of ninety (90) days following delivery, each Deliverable will conform in all material respects to its documentation. Customer's remedy for breach of this warranty is, at Vendor's option, re-performance, repair or replacement, or a refund of the fees paid for the non-conforming Services or Deliverable.

content.text:
**Finding: missing (insurance clause absent) — redline validated and submitted.**

- **Investigation:** A full-text search for "insurance" returned zero hits, and the section outline contains no insurance heading — the Agreement is entirely silent on coverage.
- **Direction check:** The gap runs against us. IBM is the hosting/services provider: § 5.3 (Security) confirms IBM implements security features for the e-business Hosting Environment and Customer Components, § 14.12 leaves risk of loss for Base Components with IBM, and § 14.18 confirms IBM processes personal information on Customer's behalf. That squarely triggers the rule's "vendor that processes personal data" trigger — indeed, no insurance here is the playbook's walk-away scenario.
- **Redline:** Inserted a new § 14.12A "Insurance" immediately after Risk of Loss (the nearest related clause, per the planner hint), at the preferred level: CGL USD 1M per occurrence / 2M aggregate, E&O USD 2M, cyber liability USD 5M for IBM's processing of Customer data, statutory workers' compensation, and certificates on request. Model language was adapted to the document's "IBM"/"Customer" naming conventions rather than "Vendor."
- **Fallback preserved:** The comment flags that we can accept E&O USD 1M / cyber USD 2M, giving negotiating room without conceding the clause itself.

input.quote: b. paying the applicable early termination charges, if any, specified in Attachment A and applicable Service Option Attachments.
input.rationale: Section 3.4(b) requires Customer to pay open-ended "early termination charges" fixed in Attachment A / Service Option Attachments, with no cap or definition in the Agreement; Section 10 further preserves IBM's recovery of "amounts owing for Services that would have been rendered but for Customer's breach". These are liquidated-type amounts payable by Customer, contrary to the preferred position of no Customer-payable liquidated damages or penalties, and potentially approaching the remaining contract value (walk-away territory). No service-credit remedy runs in our favour (11.1 imposes only Customer support obligations). Because the early-termination charge is an established commercial term of a facilities services deal, we take the fallback: cap it at three months' recurring Charges and make it the sole liquidated amount on termination.

Parties: we represent Bluefly, Inc. (Customer); counterparty is International Business Machines Corporation (IBM).

Rule:
ID: LD
Title: Liquidated damages and penalties payable by Customer
Kind: direction
Summary: Service credits to us are welcome; liquidated damages against us are not.
Severity: high
Category: commercial
Position — preferred:
No liquidated damages or penalties payable by Customer.
Position — fallback:
Early-termination fee capped at 3 months' fees as the sole liquidated amount.
Position — walk-away:
Liquidated damages exceeding the remaining contract value or triggered by minor breaches.
Detection guidance:
Identify liquidated damages, penalties, minimum fees on termination, "shall pay … as liquidated damages". Flag only when Customer pays. Service credits or LDs payable by Vendor to Customer are compliant.

Redline guidance:
Delete the Customer-payable LD; if an early-termination fee is unavoidable, cap it at 3 months' fees.

Rule:
ID: TRANSITION
Title: Post-termination transition assistance and data return
Kind: missing
Summary: When it ends, we get our data back and help moving.
Severity: medium
Category: transition
Position — preferred:
On expiry or termination, Vendor provides transition assistance for up to 6 months at then-current rates, returns Customer Data in a standard machine-readable format within 30 days, and certifies deletion thereafter.

90 days of transition assistance; data export within 30 days.
Position — walk-away:
No data return, or immediate deletion of Customer Data on termination.
Detection guidance:
Look for transition, exit, data return/export, deletion timing. Absence in a services/hosting agreement is a deviation (insert).
Redline guidance:
Insert a transition-assistance and data-return paragraph in the termination section.
Model language:
Upon expiry or termination of this Agreement for any reason, Vendor shall (a) at Customer's request, provide reasonable transition assistance for up to six (6) months at Vendor's then-current rates; (b) within thirty (30) days, return all Customer Data in a commonly used, machine-readable format; and (c) thereafter delete Customer Data from its systems and certify such deletion in writing.

content.text:
**Finding: Deviation (medium) — Warranty and duration, §§ 5.1 / 5.4**

**What the document does today**
- § 5.1(a) gives only a "reasonable care and skill" services standard (with a professional-custom gloss) plus a personnel commitment; § 5.1(b) is corporate authority; the closing covenant is limited to "laws applicable to IBM's business."
- There is **no conformance warranty** for Materials/deliverables, **no warranty period**, and **no remedy** (no re-performance, repair, replacement or refund).
- No malicious-code warranty.
- § 5.4(c) provides **all Materials "AS IS", without warranty of any kind**, which largely swallows the express commitment — close to the playbook walk-away position. §§ 5.4(a)–(b) and 5.3(b) add further disclaimers (no error-free operation, no capacity/performance/scalability, no secure operation).
- § 5.2 exclusivity is acceptable in itself, since it preserves § 5.1.

**Redline submitted (validated ok:true)**
1. Insert after p0062 — new § 5.1(c)/(d): 90-day conformance-to-documentation warranty for each Material/deliverable; no malicious code introduced by IBM; and an express remedy at IBM's option of re-performance, repair/replacement, or refund of fees paid for the non-conforming item.
2. Amend § 5.4(c) (p0074) — prefix "EXCEPT AS EXPRESSLY WARRANTED IN SECTION 5.1," so the "AS IS" disclaimer no longer overrides the express warranty.

**Fallback offered in the comment:** 30 days for Services if 90 is resisted, but a conformance warranty with a real remedy for deliverables is not waivable.

ops.text: Upon expiry or termination of this Agreement or any Service Option Attachment for any reason, IBM shall: (a) at Customer's request, provide reasonable transition assistance for up to six (6) months at IBM's then-current rates; (b) within thirty (30) days of Customer's request, return to Customer all Content and other Customer data in IBM's possession or control in a commonly used, machine-readable format; and (c) thereafter delete such Content and Customer data from its systems and certify such deletion to Customer in writing.

segments.text: Upon the date of termination, all Customer payment obligations accrued hereunder through the date of termination will become due and payable. The termination of selected Service Option Attachments will not affect Customer's obligation to pay charges under other Service Option Attachments.

messages.content:
Parties: we represent Bluefly, Inc. (Customer); counterparty is International Business Machines Corporation (IBM).

Rule:
ID: TRANSITION
Title: Post-termination transition assistance and data return
Kind: missing
Summary: When it ends, we get our data back and help moving.
Severity: medium
Category: transition
Position — preferred:
On expiry or termination, Vendor provides transition assistance for up to 6 months at then-current rates, returns Customer Data in a standard machine-readable format within 30 days, and certifies deletion thereafter.

Position — fallback:
90 days of transition assistance; data export within 30 days.
Position — walk-away:
No data return, or immediate deletion of Customer Data on termination.
Detection guidance:
Look for transition, exit, data return/export, deletion timing. Absence in a services/hosting agreement is a deviation (insert).
Redline guidance:
Insert a transition-assistance and data-return paragraph in the termination section.
Model language:
Upon expiry or termination of this Agreement for any reason, Vendor shall (a) at Customer's request, provide reasonable transition assistance for up to six (6) months at Vendor's then-current rates; (b) within thirty (30) days, return all Customer Data in a commonly used, machine-readable format; and (c) thereafter delete Customer Data from its systems and certify such deletion in writing.

Rule:
ID: MINCOMMIT
Title: Minimum purchase commitments and volume restrictions on Customer
Kind: presence
Summary: We do not take-or-pay without an exit.
Severity: medium
Category: commercial
Position — preferred:
No minimum commitment; fees are for usage or ordered services only.
Position — fallback:
Commitment limited to the current 12-month term, reducible on 30 days' notice, with a true-up rather than a penalty.
Position — walk-away:
Multi-year take-or-pay commitments with no reduction or termination right.
Detection guidance:
"minimum", "commit to purchase", "take or pay", "shortfall", volume caps on Customer usage. Commitments the Vendor makes to us are fine.
Redline guidance:
Delete or narrow to the fallback with minimal edits; replace shortfall penalties with a true-up.

content.text:
**Finding submitted: deviation (high severity, § 3.4(b))**

- **Issue:** § 3.4(b) makes Customer pay undefined, uncapped "early termination charges" set in Attachment A / Service Option Attachments — a Customer-payable liquidated amount. § 10 (p0123) reinforces this by carving out from the consequential-damages waiver "amounts owing for Services that would have been rendered but for Customer's breach," i.e. unaccrued future fees.
- **Direction check:** These amounts run against us; § 3.3 only removes them where IBM breaches. There is no service-credit or LD remedy in our favour (§ 11.1 imposes only Customer support duties), so nothing here is compliant-by-direction.
- **Redline (fallback, validated ok:true):** caps the early termination charge at three (3) months' recurring Charges for the terminated Services, makes it IBM's sole and exclusive remedy for the termination, and confirms no liquidated damages, penalty, or unaccrued/future charges are payable by Customer. Fallback rather than outright deletion because the early-termination charge is an established commercial term of this facilities services deal.

input.quote: Charges for applicable Services will be specified in Service Option Attachments and Order Forms. Charges can be specified as one-time, installment, recurring, or usage. IBM will invoice such Charges when they begin or are due as set forth in Service Option Attachments.
input.rationale: The Base Terms impose no minimum purchase commitment, committed volume, take-or-pay or shortfall charge on Customer. Section 4.1 (p0052) ties Charges solely to Services specified in Service Option Attachments and Order Forms (one-time, installment, recurring or usage), and Section 11.5 Capacity Planning (p0142) only allocates responsibility for sizing decisions to Customer rather than committing Customer to any capacity or volume. Customer also retains a monthly termination for convenience right on one month's notice (p0044–p0045), so no take-or-pay lock-in exists. This meets our preferred position, so no redline is proposed. Residual watch item only (outside this rule): Section 3.4(b) preserves "early termination charges, if any, specified in Attachment A and applicable Service Option Attachments" (p0046) — those attachments are not part of this document, and we should confirm at Order Form stage that any such charge is a true-up of amounts for services actually ordered rather than a penalty or disguised minimum commitment.

Multi-year take-or-pay commitments with no reduction or termination right.

"minimum", "commit to purchase", "take or pay", "shortfall", volume caps on Customer usage. Commitments the Vendor makes to us are fine.

Delete or narrow to the fallback with minimal edits; replace shortfall penalties with a true-up.

content.text:
**Finding: Compliant** (no redline proposed)

- **§ 4.1 Charges (p0052)** ties all Charges to Services actually specified in Order Forms / Service Option Attachments on a one-time, installment, recurring or usage basis — no minimum, committed volume, take-or-pay or shortfall mechanic anywhere in the Base Terms (searches for "minimum", "commit", "shortfall", "volume" returned nothing relevant).
- **§ 11.5 Capacity Planning (p0142)** only allocates sizing/forecasting responsibility to Customer; it does not commit us to any capacity level or usage volume.
- **§ 3.4 (p0044–p0045)** gives us a convenience exit at the end of any calendar month on one month's notice, so there is no lock-in even if an Order Form were to include a term.

This satisfies the preferred position, so no edit was made. One watch item flagged for the Order Form stage (not a deviation in this document): § 3.4(b) preserves "early termination charges, if any, specified in Attachment A and applicable Service Option Attachments" — those documents are not before us, and we should confirm any such charge is a true-up for services actually ordered rather than a penalty or disguised minimum commitment.

**Finding: missing (medium)** — no transition/exit rights anywhere in the Agreement.

- § 3.5 "Effect of Termination" covers only accrued payment obligations; nothing on wind-down, transition help, or data.
- Full-text searches for "transition", "export", "delete", "Customer Data" return no hits; "return" appears only in the IP indemnity (§ 8.1) and the signature block. §§ 11.6 and 14.18 merely allocate responsibility for Content and contact information — they give us no return or deletion right.
- Fix: inserted a new § 3.5.1 requiring IBM to (a) provide up to 6 months' transition assistance at then-current rates, (b) return all Content/Customer data in a machine-readable format within 30 days, and (c) then delete and certify deletion. § 14.2 already lists § 3.5 as surviving, so no further edit was needed.
- Fallback offered in the comment: 90 days of assistance with the same 30-day export.

{"markdown":"# Issues Memo — IBM Facilities/Hosted Services Agreement

**To:** Deal team
**From:** In-house counsel (Customer side)
**Re:** Playbook review of the Agreement (Base Terms), including § 3.1 Term
**Status of findings:** Verified findings as supplied; verification step recorded as skipped for each item.

---

## Executive summary

We have reviewed the Agreement against our playbook and identified 19 findings: three critical deviations, six high-severity items (four deviations, two compliant), eight medium items (four deviations, one missing, three compliant), and one low-severity gap.

The commercial shape of the deal is workable, but the risk allocation is materially one-sided in IBM's favour in three respects. First, on **liability** (§ 9.1), the cap floor is $100,000 measured on charges "paid" only, there are no carve-outs for confidentiality, data protection, gross negligence, wilful misconduct or fraud, and § 9.1(c)(2) excludes IBM's liability entirely for loss of or damage to our records and data — the core risk in a hosting arrangement. Second, on **IP** (§ 5.4 / Section 7), the default is IBM-owned Type II Materials with a narrow internal-use licence back to us, while for Materials we do own IBM receives an irrevocable, worldwide licence to distribute externally; there is no express statement that we retain ownership of Content or Customer Components. Third, on **indemnities** (§ 8.1–8.2), IBM gives an IP infringement indemnity only, while our indemnity at 8.2(3) extends to any Services Recipient claim relating directly or indirectly to IBM's own Services — a one-way indemnity for the Vendor's services.

On **exit**, our termination for convenience right (§ 3.4) is conditioned on uncapped, undefined early termination charges, with no refund of prepaid Charges anywhere in the Agreement, and § 3.5 contains no transition assistance, data return, export or deletion obligations. Renewal (§ 3.2) auto-renews for a term equal to the prior term (permitting automatic multi-year renewals) on 90 days' notice, with no cap on renewal Charges.

On the positive side, the Agreement imposes **no exclusivity, non-compete, MFN, minimum purchase commitment or employee non-solicitation** on us, and § 14.16 (Freedom of Action) affirmatively preserves our ability to source competing services. Governing law is New York, which is our preferred position; the only gap is the absence of a forum/venue provision.

---

## Findings table

| # | Severity | Rule | Status | Section |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Critical | INDEMN — Indemnification by Vendor | Deviation | § 8.1 Indemnification by IBM |
| 2 | Critical | IP — Ownership of deliverables and Customer Data | Deviation | § 5.4 Other Disclaimers |
| 3 | Critical | LOL-CAP — Limitation of liability: cap, mutuality, carve-outs | Deviation | § 9.1 IBM's Limitation of Liability |
| 4 | High | ASSIGN — Assignment and change of control | Deviation | § 14.10 Assignment |
| 5 | High | LD — Liquidated damages/penalties payable by Customer | Deviation | § 3.4 Termination for Convenience |
| 6 | High | LICENSE — Licence grant scope | Deviation | § 12.1 License |
| 7 | High | T4C — Termination for convenience | Deviation | § 3.4 Termination for Convenience |
| 8 | High | EXCLUSIVITY — Exclusivity obligations binding Customer | Compliant | § 14.16 Freedom of Action |
| 9 | High | NONCOMPETE — Non-compete restrictions on Customer | Compliant | § 14.16 Freedom of Action |
| 10 | Medium | AUDIT — Audit rights against Customer | Deviation | § 11.3 Suspected Violations |
| 11 | Medium | GOVLAW — Governing law and venue | Deviation | § 14.3 Choice of Law |
| 12 | Medium | RENEWAL — Auto-renewal and non-renewal notice window | Deviation | § 3.2 Renewal |
| 13 | Medium | WARRANTY — Performance warranty and duration | Deviation | § 5.1 IBM Representations and Warranties |
| 14 | Medium | TRANSITION — Post-termination transition assistance and data return | Missing | § 3.5 Effect of Termination |
| 15 | Medium | MFN — Most-favoured-nation obligations burdening Customer | Compliant | § 14.16 Freedom of Action |
| 16 | Medium | MINCOMMIT — Minimum purchase commitments/volume restrictions | Compliant | § 4.1 Charges |
| 17 | Medium | NOSOLICIT — Non-solicitation of employees binding Customer | Compliant | § 14.8 Personnel |
| 18 | Low | INSURANCE — Vendor insurance | Missing | § 14.12 Risk of Loss |

---

## Walk-away items

The following findings were assessed as at or approaching our playbook walk-away line. We should not sign without movement on these:

1. **One-way indemnity for IBM's own Services (§ 8.2(3)).** Our indemnity covers any Services Recipient claim relating directly or indirectly to IBM's Services, only partially offset by the carve-back in 8.2(c). We propose narrowing this to our breach of applicable law, leaving the Content/AUP and mechanics' lien prongs intact.
2. **Exclusion of IBM liability for loss of or damage to our records and data (§ 9.1(c)(2)).** In a hosting deal this excludes the central risk, and § 6 reinforces it by giving §§ 5, 9 and 10 precedence over the confidentiality agreement. We propose deleting the exclusion, raising the mutual cap floor to $1,000,000 on fees paid or payable, and adding a mutual uncapped carve-out sentence.
3. **At-will revocable licence (§ 12.1).** The Base Components licence is expressly "revocable" with no breach or cure predicate, and § 14.17 confirms no rights beyond those expressly granted. We propose limiting revocation to uncured material breach and extending the grant to Affiliates and contractors acting on our behalf.
4. **Uncapped early termination charges (§ 3.4(b), with § 10).** The charges are undefined in the Agreement and cross-referenced to attachments not before us, potentially approaching remaining contract value. Fallback: cap at three months' recurring Charges as the sole liquidated amount on termination.
5. **Automatic multi-year renewal (§ 3.2).** Renewal for a term equal in duration to the prior term, with no cap on renewal Charges. We propose fixing renewals at 12 months with 30 days' notice, a 60-day reminder and a CPI/3% uplift cap.
6. **Unlimited, unannounced investigation right (§ 11.3).** No frequency, notice, business-hours, confidentiality or cost limits, and no exclusion of access to our systems. Fallback: 15 days' notice / 10% threshold formulation.
7. **"AS IS" disclaimer swallowing the express warranty (§ 5.4(c) with § 5.1).** IBM warrants only reasonable care and skill, with no conformance warranty, warranty period or remedy for Materials.

---

## Next steps

1. **Issue the redline.** The proposed changes are drafted for §§ 3.2, 3.4, 3.5, 5.1, 5.4(c), 8.1, 8.2(3), 9.1, 11.3, 12.1, 14.3, 14.10 and a new § 14.12A (insurance), plus the Section 7 Materials ownership flip to Type I with a broadened Type II licence-back and an express Customer Data/Content ownership and no-joint-ownership statement.
2. **Prioritise negotiation** in the order set out above: liability and data-loss exclusion, IP ownership, indemnity symmetry, then exit economics (early termination charges, prepaid refund, transition assistance).
3. **Obtain the missing attachments.** Attachment A and the Service Option Attachments govern Charges and early termination charges but are not part of this document. We should confirm at Order Form stage that any early termination charge is a true-up for services actually ordered rather than a penalty or disguised minimum commitment (per the MINCOMMIT watch item).
4. **Confirm insurance appetite** with IBM, offering the fallback of E&O USD 1M / cyber USD 2M against our opening position of CGL USD 1M/2M, E&O USD 2M, cyber USD 5M and statutory workers' compensation, with certificates on request.
5. **Complete verification.** Verification was skipped for all findings; we should re-run confirmation of section references against the executed form before the redline is exchanged.
6. **Preserve the compliant positions.** No changes are needed to §§ 14.16, 14.8, 14.11 or 4.1, and we should resist any counter-proposal that introduces exclusivity, MFN, minimum volume or non-solicit obligations on us."}
